title: The CMIP7Plus AMIP SST forcing built from DOISST v2.1 keeps the DOISST input steps; in five Green's functions they cause about 70% of its excess 2001-2022 radiative cooling
abstract: Question: in August 2025 PCMDI published new AMIP SST forcings for CMIP7Plus, each from one product. PCMDI-AMIP-OI2p1-1-0 uses DOISST v2.1, which has false warm steps at input changes (2005-01-01, 2020-07-07). In E3SMv2 AMIP runs (Zelinka et al. 2024) the OISST v2.1 run was the 2001-2022 outlier: more warming (0.26 against 0.15-0.18 K per decade) and a negative fixed-forcing TOA trend (-0.13 against +0.10 to +0.20 W m-2 per decade). Do the DOISST steps cause this? What causes the 2018 cold step in OI v2 (PCMDI-AMIP-1-1-9)? Approach: we compared the OI2p1, ERSST5, Had1p1 and 1-1-9 forcings on the global ocean, removed the DOISST box steps (fitted to in situ data or to ESA CCI) from OI2p1, and applied the Jacobians of five atmosphere models (GFMIP). We compared OI v2 with DOISST v2.0 (526 days from NCEI). Results: OI2p1 equals DOISST v2.1 (RMS 0.003 K) and has steps of +0.08 to +0.10 K. Its 2001-2022 global-ocean SST trend is 0.173 K per decade (other forcings 0.099-0.139); corrected 0.115-0.129. The corrections remove 73-97% of its excess warming and 69-77% of its excess Green's-function TOA trend (-0.330 against a sibling mean of -0.188; corrected -0.221 to -0.233 W m-2 per decade). The steps act as near-uniform warming. Over 1982-2022 OI2p1 gives almost no pattern effect (+0.03 W m-2 K-1 against -0.14 to -0.24). The Green's functions give 36-71% of the E3SM differences, with the same sign. OI v2 drifts cold against v2.1 in 2016-2020 at the same time and in a similar pattern (r = 0.46) as DOISST v2.0, which lost drifting-buoy data in the NCEP TAC stream; OI v2 shows 40-50% of that drift. Limitations: E3SM values are from slides and single runs; Green's functions are linear and do not include E3SM; corrections are uncertain by up to a factor of two; a pre-2005 drift and the 2005 polar ice step are not corrected; the OI v2 cause is inferred from timing and pattern, without input counts.
